Calculate the correlation between gene expression and another variable using a linear model

Source: R/expression_correlation.R
calc_expr_corr.Rd

This function calculates the correlation between gene expression and another continuous variable, most commonly another gene. This function is used to identify the list of genes in which the expression is correlated with another variable/gene in a dose- dependent manner. This function uses a linear model to calculate the correlation, with the query gene as the independent variable and all other genes as the dependent variable. The significance of the correlation is calculated using the p-value of the linear model and is adjusted for multiple testing using a user-defined method. The slope of the linear model is used as the correlation coefficient, with R-squared as the measure of goodness of fit. The strength of the correlation is calculated using a user-defined method (e.g., Pearson, Spearman, Kendall).

Usage

calc_expr_corr(
  gene_expr,
  query_var,
  metadata = NULL,
  vars_to_regress = NULL,
  scale_expr = TRUE,
  plot_model = FALSE,
  base_dir = getwd(),
  corr_method = "pearson",
  p_adjust_method = "BH",
  file_type = "png",
  dpi = 1000,
  plot_group_var = NULL,
  switch_axes = FALSE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

gene_expr

A data frame containing the gene expression data. The data frame should have the genes as rows and samples as columns. The gene expression data should be normalized (e.g. CPM) and consist of only numeric values. All genes in this data frame, except the query gene, will be used as the dependent variable in the linear model. However, the query_var can also be specified in the metadata data frame. Note, only numeric values are allowed in the gene expression data.

query_var

A character string specifying the query gene for which the correlation with other genes will be calculated. The query gene should be present in the gene expression data frame, and it must be a row name in the gene_expr data frame. In general, the query gene is the gene of interest and should be a continuous variable specified in the gene_expr data frame. However, in other cases, the query gene can be a categorical/ordinal variable specified in the metadata data frame. In this case, any ordinal variable should be converted into a numeric variable before using this function. Categorical variables should be converted into a factor and have the base level set as the reference level.

metadata

A data frame containing the metadata information for the samples. The data frame should have samples as rows and metadata variables as columns. The metadata information can contain the query_var and/or vars_to_regress variables that are used as covariates in the linear model. The metadata information can be used to adjust the gene expression data for confounding variables. The metadata can contain both categorical and continuous variables. ordinal variables should be converted into numeric variables before using this function. Categorical variables should be converted into a factor and have the base level set as the reference level. Default value is NULL. Note, row names of the metadata data frame should match the column names of the gene_expr data frame.

vars_to_regress

A character vector specifying the variables to regress out from the linear model. The default value is NULL, which means no variables will be regressed out. The variables can present in either the gene_expr or metadata data frame. However, if the variable are not continuous, they should only exist in the metadata data frame.

scale_expr

A logical value indicating whether to scale the gene expression data before calculating the correlation. If TRUE, the gene expression data will be scaled using the scale function to a mean of 0 and a standard deviation of 1 (z-score). Expression of each gene will be scaled independently across samples. The default value is TRUE. If false, the original gene expression data will be used for calculations.

plot_model

A logical value indicating whether to plot the linear model for each gene. The default value is FALSE. If true, a plot will be generated for each gene showing the linear model with the query gene on the x-axis and the gene expression on the y-axis. The plot will also show the linear model coefficients, R-squared value, correlation coefficient, and FDR-adjusted p-value. The plot will be a ggplot object and can be further customized using the ggplot2 functions. The plot will be saved in the model_plots_positive and model_plots_negative directories in the base_dir directory.

base_dir

A character string specifying the base directory to save the model results and plots. The default value is the current working directory. The model results will be saved as a CSV file named query_var_correlation_results.csv.

corr_method

A character string specifying the method to calculate the correlation. The available methods include "pearson", "spearman", "kendall". The default method is "pearson".

p_adjust_method

A character string specifying the method to adjust the p-values for multiple testing. The available methods include "BH" (Benjamini-Hochberg), "bonferroni", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "BY", "fdr", "none". The default method is "BH". See p.adjust for more details.

file_type

A character string specifying the file type for the model plots. The available file types include "png", "jpeg", "tiff", "pdf", "svg". The default file type is "png".

dpi

An integer specifying the resolution of raster plots (e.g. png) in dots per inch (DPI). The default value is 1000. The DPI value should be greater than 0.

plot_group_var

A character string specifying the variable in the metadata data frame to group the samples in the plot.

switch_axes

A logical value indicating whether to switch the axes of the plot. The default value is FALSE. If TRUE, the query gene will be plotted on the y-axis and the gene expression on the x-axis.

alpha

The significance level for the adjusted p-values. The default value is 0.05.

verbose

A logical value indicating whether to print the progress messages. The default value is TRUE.

Value

A list of four elements:

model_list

A list of linear models for each gene, with the query gene as the independent variable and the gene expression as the dependent variable.

model_results

A data frame containing the correlation results, including the correlation coefficient, p-value, adjusted p-value, and R-squared value for each gene.

p_volcano

A ggplot object of the volcano plot showing the correlation results.

pos_plots

A list containing the ggplot objects for each gene showing the linear model plot. The plots will be saved automatically. Only available if plot_model is TRUE.

neg_plots

A list containing the ggplot objects for each gene showing the linear model plot. The plots will be saved automatically. Only available if plot_model is TRUE.
